label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Sizwe, congratulations on the wedding first — sorry man, this is a hell of a Friday night.

Straight answer: leave the key OUT of that bakkie. Put it in your pocket, or on a windowsill 50 m away. Do not turn it one more time tonight.

Every time it cranks, the high pressure pump is running on petrol with zero lube in it. You already stalled and cranked it 5 or 6 times, so damage is possible. Don't top it up with diesel either — the petrol's still in the tank, mixing does nothing.

Kobus, with respect, that's old Land Rover advice. Modern common rail will not drink petrol and drive off into the sunset.

Tonight:
1. Key stays out. That's it.
2. Check your insurance policy for roadside/TOW before you pay any tow guy cash.
3. Get it TOWED, don't drive it. Straight to a diesel shop, pump and injectors first.

If the pump and injectors are fine, then it's: drain tank, flush lines, new fuel filter, bleed the system. Usually R2 500 to R4 500 all in. Can't promise a total tonight, so don't sit and wait for a number.

My shop's in Umbilo, open Sat 7 till 12. Thabo, my guy, can start draining it first thing — ring me tonight and I'll have him there early.

And ha, one customer did this to me TWICE in the same year, same garage. We ended up making him a sticker for the fuel flap. Also my first year as apprentice in 1995 I put diesel in the boss's Golf — he still tells that story at every braai. So you're in good company, you'll be telling this one for the next 20 years.

One more thing: borrow a bakkie for the sound system and the cake anyway. Don't plan the wedding around a drained tank, nobody wants a flatbed pulling up at the venue.

Leave that key alone. Phone me.
